tables.name: weekly_hours
tables.description: Weekly open hours (H01; FS schedule row, kind hours): one row per open span on one day of the week, for a location (its opening hours, H01), a bookable resource (a worker's own hours, at one of the business's locations or any; a room's or vehicle's) or a space or thing (S1-81: 'A space has its own hours'). tables.name: time_off
tables.description: Time off, closed days and blocked times (H02; FS schedule row, kind time off): a window of instants in which an owner of hours (the whole business, a location, a resource, or a space or thing) takes no new bookings. A team member's day off asked by text waits for the owner's OK, and new bookings with them in it pause meanwhile (S11-43, S11-44); the owner's BLOCK takes effect on the read-back's yes (S11-13); a space or room closed for a day (S1-81, S1-83). Visits already booked inside it stay until the owner picks what happens to them (S11-13, S11-106); their reservations are K-04's. No reason is kept: a reason can be a health detail (RULES 4.5).

tables.name: calendar_links
tables.description: A person's own calendar linked to Rosie (H03; S1-24; S2-06): Google or Microsoft, busy times only. A link is the person's, never one business's: one person has one calendar across every company (S1-24; FS line 743; K-16 v1 calendarLinkId), so a person has one live link, with one change subscription (one Google channel or one Graph subscription) and one set of busy blocks, and each business they work in reads it through its own calendar_link_shares row (S1-38's carry-over adds one, never asking twice), seeing only free or busy through it. It holds only what the database needs: the person, the provider, the state, the sync marks (the provider's cursor and change subscription) and the OAuth tokens, sealed under the person's key. The row is written when the person starts connecting, with no tokens yet, and the connect's return seals the tokens into it (K-16 v1 connectStart, connectReturn). No secure link is texted to connect or reconnect it (MC 8 'Calendars'; Q-10).
tables.source: FS row H03 ('Calendar link per person (Rosie sees only busy times)'); FS lines 723 (staff.calendar_link), 743 ('one calendar'); S1-24 (gives calendar: 'One person has one calendar across every kind of work and company'; 'Each person can link their own calendar when they join'); S1-38 ('The ID, mobile, calendar and bill card carry over, never asked twice'); S2-02, S2-06; arch 05 lines 261, 265, 271; arch 11 lines 578, 580; S12-13, S12-14; MC 8 'Calendars'; Q-10, Q-11, Q-56; 02-contracts row K-27 ('calendar links per person') and section 8 (calendar: K-27); K-16 v1 calendarLinkId ('a link belongs to a person, never to one business'), connectStart.request, tokensKept, watch.response

columns.name: id
columns.description: The link's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09); K-16 v1's calendarLinkId.
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings); K-16 v1 calendarLinkId

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: Whose calendar (persons.id); their key in K-04 sealing_keys seals the tokens. Each person links their own, and has at most one live link (calendar_links_one_live_per_person).
columns.source: S1-24 ('Each person can link their own calendar when they join'; 'One person has one calendar across every kind of work and company'); arch 05 line 261 ('Each person links their own calendar'); FS line 743; K-16 v1 connectStart.request personId

columns.name: provider
columns.description: google or microsoft (Microsoft 365 and Outlook). Apple iCloud is not linked (Q-11).
columns.source: MC 8 'Calendars' ('Google and Microsoft, two-way, busy times only'); arch 05 line 261; Q-11

columns.name: state
columns.description: connecting: the person started connecting on a page they already have open (K-16 v1 connectStart: 'The caller (C-189) writes the link row first'), so the row exists with no tokens yet and nothing is read or watched; it takes no time out of offer (S1-24's safe default: 'nothing blocked yet'), and a start not finished, or declined, leaves it connecting for the next start to reuse. linked: the connect's return sealed the tokens (K-16 v1 connectReturn, tokensKept), and busy times are read in (arch 05 line 261). dropped: its change subscription could not be renewed after the effects retries, or the provider refused its tokens, so that person's open times are not offered at any business that reads the link until it is reconnected; booked visits stay and the rest of the team is still offered (arch 05 line 271; arch 11 line 580; S12-13); a reconnect leaves it dropped until the return. unlinked: ended (the person took it off, left every team that reads it, or linked another calendar), its tokens erased and its busy blocks deleted.
columns.source: K-16 v1 connectStart.request, connectReturn.response, tokensKept; S1-24 (safe default: 'nothing blocked yet, with one reminder'); arch 05 line 271 ('a renewal still failing after section 10's Effects retries is a dropped link'); arch 11 line 580; S12-13, S12-14; RULES 8.7

columns.name: tokens
columns.description: The provider's OAuth tokens (the refresh token, and the access token with its expiry) as one value sealed under the person's key in K-04 sealing_keys (arch 05 line 271: 'Links keep their tokens sealed under the person's key'), never plain and never in a message, log or trace. Only the runtime side writes it: the calendar adapter seals it at the connect's return and seals each refresh again (K-16 v1 tokensKept: 'The adapter seals and keeps them at connectReturn'), and the Tool API can neither read nor write it (README rule 5). Null while connecting and once unlinked. Its inner form is K-16's.
columns.source: arch 05 line 271; arch 01 line 93; BP rule 7; RULES 4.10; 02-contracts K-16 ('the tokens sealed under the person's key'); K-16 v1 tokensKept, connectReturn.response (tokens: sealedUnderPersonKey); migration 0003 (sealing_keys reached only from the runtime side)

columns.name: linked_at
columns.description: When the connect's return sealed the tokens (K-16 v1 connectReturn linkedAt), first or at a reconnect; null while connecting, and on a link unlinked before it was ever linked.
columns.source: S1-24 ('Connected'); K-16 v1 connectReturn.response linkedAt; S12-13, S12-14 (reconnect)

columns.name: sync_cursor
columns.description: Where the next read of changes starts: Google's sync token or Microsoft's delta link; null before the first full read, or after the provider refuses it, so the next read is a full one.
columns.source: arch 05 line 261 ('read with sync tokens'; 'read with delta queries'); 02-contracts K-16 ('Watch and renew')

columns.name: synced_at
columns.description: When the last read of changes finished (after a push, the 30-minute poll or a full read); a linked person's times are offered only up to 90 days after it. Null before the first; a reconnect's return nulls it with sync_cursor, since the return moves linked_at past it (calendar_links_times_in_order) and everything since the drop is read again.
columns.source: arch 05 line 265 ('Rosie reads 90 days ahead ... and never offers a linked person's time past that'); arch 11 lines 578 (the 30-minute poll), 580 (a reconnect reads everything since)

columns.name: subscription_id
columns.description: The change subscription: Google's channel id or Microsoft Graph's subscription id, by which a notification finds this link; null while it has none.
columns.source: arch 05 line 261 ('Google sends change notifications'; 'Graph change notifications'); arch 05 line 271

columns.name: subscription_resource_id
columns.description: Google's resource id for the watched calendar, which stopping the channel needs; null for Microsoft, or with no subscription. Its writer is K-16 v1.1's watch and renew answers (lead card T-1082): K-16 v1's answers do not carry it, so until then it stays null.
columns.source: arch 05 line 261; 02-contracts K-16 ('Watch and renew'); K-16 v1 README spike row 1 (channels/stop with id and resourceId); lead card T-1082

columns.name: subscribed_at
columns.description: When the current subscription started or was last renewed; null with subscription_id.
columns.source: arch 05 line 271 ('renewed when half its life is left')

columns.name: subscription_expires_at
columns.description: When the current subscription expires. It is renewed when half its life is left, at subscribed_at plus half of (subscription_expires_at - subscribed_at); null with subscription_id.
columns.source: arch 05 line 271

columns.name: dropped_at
columns.description: When it dropped; the owner of each business that reads it is texted at once (S12-13). Null unless dropped; a reconnect's return clears it.
columns.source: arch 11 line 580 ('The owner is texted at once'); S12-13

columns.name: dropped_why
columns.description: renewal_failed: a renewal still failing after the effects retries (arch 05 line 271; arch 10 line 542); access_refused: the provider refused its tokens, so nothing can be read. Set with dropped_at.
columns.source: arch 05 line 271; arch 10 line 542; S12-13 ('stopped sharing with Rosie')

columns.name: drop_reminded_at
columns.description: When the one reminder went, the link still not reconnected 24 hours after it dropped; null: not yet.
columns.source: arch 11 line 580 ('Not reconnected in 24 hours: one reminder'); S12-14

columns.name: unlinked_at
columns.description: When it was unlinked; null unless unlinked.
columns.source: RULES 8.7 (access ends when a person leaves); S11-49

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and each write (a sync mark, a renewal, a token refresh, a drop, a reconnect) compares and sets it, so two writers of one link never both move it. One version covers the tokens and the sync marks: a token refresh during a call raises it, so a caller whose compare-and-set of the cursor or the subscription then fails with versionChanged re-reads the row and applies its write again (safe: the same cursor reads the same changes, K-16 v1 readChanges).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2; K-16 v1 tokensKept (refresh and seal again), readChanges.request ('Repeating it with the same cursor is safe')

unique.name: calendar_links_one_live_per_person
unique.source: FS row H03 ('Calendar link per person'); FS line 743 ('one calendar'); S1-24 ('One person has one calendar across every kind of work and company'); 02-contracts row K-27 ('calendar links per person'); K-16 v1 calendarLinkId, watch.response (one person has one link)

unique.name: calendar_links_subscription_key
unique.source: arch 05 line 261 (a notification names its channel or subscription); K-16 v1 README default 16 (Graph's 409 answers the person's one subscription)

unique.name: calendar_links_id_person_key
unique.source: S1-24 (each person links their own): a share and a busy block keep their link's person (calendar_link_shares_link_fk, busy_blocks_link_fk)

checks.name: calendar_links_provider_known
checks.source: MC 8 'Calendars' ('Google and Microsoft'); Q-11 (Apple iCloud not linked); 02-contracts K-16 refuse-icloud

checks.name: calendar_links_state_known
checks.source: K-16 v1 connectStart.request (the row written first), connectReturn.response; arch 05 line 271; arch 11 line 580

checks.name: calendar_links_tokens_while_live
checks.source: K-16 v1 tokensKept ('The adapter seals and keeps them at connectReturn'); arch 05 line 271 (tokens sealed); RULES 4.10 (nothing kept that is no longer needed)

checks.name: calendar_links_linked_has_time
checks.expression: (state <> 'connecting' or linked_at is null) and (state not in ('linked', 'dropped') or linked_at is not null)

checks.name: calendar_links_connecting_unread
checks.expression: state <> 'connecting' or (sync_cursor is null and synced_at is null and subscription_id is null)
checks.source: K-16 v1 connectReturn.response ('the caller then starts the link's watch and its first read'): a link with no tokens yet is never read or watched

checks.name: calendar_links_dropped_has_time
checks.expression: (state = 'dropped') = (dropped_at is not null) and (dropped_at is null) = (dropped_why is null) and (dropped_why is null or dropped_why in ('renewal_failed', 'access_refused'))

checks.name: calendar_links_reminded_while_dropped
checks.expression: drop_reminded_at is null or (state = 'dropped' and drop_reminded_at >= dropped_at)

checks.name: calendar_links_subscription_whole
checks.expression: (subscription_id is null) = (subscribed_at is null) and (subscription_id is null) = (subscription_expires_at is null) and (subscription_resource_id is null or subscription_id is not null) and (subscription_expires_at is null or subscription_expires_at > subscribed_at) and (state <> 'unlinked' or subscription_id is null)

checks.name: calendar_links_times_in_order
checks.expression: (dropped_at is null or dropped_at >= linked_at) and (unlinked_at is null or unlinked_at >= linked_at) and (synced_at is null or synced_at >= linked_at)

indexes.name: calendar_links_renewal_idx
indexes.where: state = 'linked' and subscription_id is not null
indexes.why: The links whose subscription nears half its life, for renewal (arch 05 line 271).

indexes.name: calendar_links_person_idx
indexes.why: A person's links, live and unlinked: S1-38's carry-over finds the live one, erasure finds them all (FS line 743; RULES 4.10).

rowLevelSecurity.why: A link is a person's, across every business they work in (S1-24: 'One person has one calendar across every kind of work and company'; FS line 743; K-16 v1 calendarLinkId: 'a link belongs to a person, never to one business'), so it has no business column. A Tool API call sees a link only through a live calendar_link_shares row of its own business, or in the call of the link's own person (K-22 v1 rosie.person_id), and never the tokens; every write is the runtime side's (README rule 5).

tables.name: calendar_link_shares
tables.description: A business that reads a person's calendar link: one row per link and business, while it reads it. A person links one calendar (S1-24; FS line 743), and each business they work in reads that one link through its own row: the business whose page the person connected on (registration screen 16, the owner console, the staff page: Q-10), and each next business S1-38's carry-over adds ('The ID, mobile, calendar and bill card carry over, never asked twice'). Through it the business sees only free or busy: the link's state and its busy blocks' times, never the tokens or what an event is (S1-24: 'Rosie sees only when Sam is busy, never what the job is'). So one change subscription and one set of busy blocks serve every business. A business stops reading it when the person takes it off that business or leaves its team (RULES 8.7): the row is ended, never deleted or reopened.
tables.source: S1-24 ('One person has one calendar across every kind of work and company'; 'Each person can link their own calendar when they join'); S1-38; S11-43 ('Each business sees only busy times from the other'); FS line 743 ('one calendar'; 'A booking in any of their businesses blocks that time in all of them'); FS row H03; arch 10 line 546; RULES 8.7; 02-contracts row K-27 ('calendar links per person'); K-16 v1 calendarLinkId

columns.name: id
columns.description: The share's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

columns.name: calendar_link_id
columns.description: The link the business reads (calendar_links.id), held to its person by calendar_link_shares_link_fk.
columns.source: S1-24; K-16 v1 calendarLinkId

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: Whose calendar (persons.id), copied from the link and held to it by calendar_link_shares_link_fk, so the Tool API's insert policy admits only the call's own person's link (README rule 5: each person shares their own).
columns.source: S1-24 ('Each person can link their own calendar when they join'); arch 05 line 261; K-22 v1 rule 4 (rosie.person_id)

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business that reads the link (businesses.id): the business whose page the person connected on, or the next business S1-38 carried it over to.

columns.name: shared_at
columns.description: When the business started reading the link: the connect's start on its page (K-16 v1 connectStart), or S1-38's carry-over.
columns.source: S1-24; S1-38; K-16 v1 connectStart.request

columns.name: ended_at
columns.description: When the business stopped reading it: the person took it off this business, left its team (RULES 8.7), linked another calendar, or the link was unlinked; null while it reads it.
columns.source: RULES 8.7 (access ends when a person leaves); S11-49

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

unique.name: calendar_link_shares_one_per_person
unique.source: S1-24 ('One person has one calendar'); FS line 743: a business reads one calendar per person, so a repeated connect start or carry-over never adds a second

checks.name: calendar_link_shares_times_in_order
checks.expression: ended_at is null or ended_at >= shared_at

indexes.name: calendar_link_shares_link_idx
indexes.why: The businesses that read a link: the read policies of calendar_links and busy_blocks (README rule 5), and a drop told to each business's owner (S12-13; C-182).

tables.name: busy_blocks
tables.description: When a person is busy, never what (S1-24: 'Rosie sees only when Sam is busy, never what the job is'): start, end and source only (arch 05 line 261). From a linked calendar, one row per busy event, or per repeat of a repeating event, read 90 days ahead (arch 05 line 265): such a block is its link's, so its person's, written once however many businesses read the link, and each of them reads it through its live calendar_link_shares row; or from a photo of the owner's schedule, one row per time read back, written only on the owner's yes (S1-24; arch 05 line 263; limit 6), for the business whose owner said it. An open time for the person at a business is outside every busy block it reads (RULES 2.6). The table has no column for a title, description, place, attendee or organizer, so none can be stored (refuse-busy-block-title).
tables.source: arch 05 lines 259, 261 ('Rosie keeps each busy block's start, end and source, never its title'), 263, 265; arch 11 line 578; S1-24 (gives calendar); S12-33 ('The event's title is never shown'); RULES 2.6; MC 8 'Calendars' ('busy times only'); 02-contracts row K-27 ('busy blocks with start, end and source, never the title'); 02-contracts K-02 v1.1 (schedule: busy times with start and end, never what the job is)

columns.name: id
columns.description: The block's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: For a photo block, the business whose owner said yes to its times, where it blocks the person (businesses.id); null for a calendar block, which is its link's, and is read by each business that reads the link through its live share (README rule 5).
columns.source: arch 10 line 546; S1-24; FS line 743; K-16 v1 calendarLinkId

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: Whose busy time (persons.id): the link's person (held to it by busy_blocks_link_fk), or, for a photo, the person whose schedule it is (S1-24: the owner's own).
columns.source: arch 05 line 261 ('the person's busy blocks'); S1-24; FS line 743

columns.name: source
columns.description: calendar: read from a linked calendar; photo: read from a photo of the schedule and confirmed by the owner.
columns.source: arch 05 lines 261 ('start, end and source'), 263

columns.name: calendar_link_id
columns.description: For a calendar block, the link it was read through (calendar_links.id), held to the same person by the foreign key; null for a photo.
columns.source: arch 05 line 261

columns.name: provider_event_ref
columns.description: For a calendar block, the provider's id for the event, or for one repeat of a repeating event: with the link, the key a change or deletion finds the row by. An opaque id, never a title, and never shown. Null for a photo.
columns.source: arch 05 line 265 ('expanding repeating events'); 02-contracts K-16 ('Read changes into busy blocks')

columns.name: during
columns.description: When the person is busy, [start, end), as instants (UTC); an all-day event spans its days in time_zone. The owner may see that a person is busy then, never what (S1-24).
columns.source: arch 05 line 265 ('Times are kept in UTC with the event's zone'); S1-24; CQ-09

columns.name: time_zone
columns.description: The event's IANA zone as the provider gives it, else its calendar's (arch 05 line 265: 'Times are kept in UTC with the event's zone'); for a photo, the zone its times were read back in (the business's).
columns.source: arch 05 line 265; CQ-05; CQ-09

columns.name: confirmed_at
columns.description: For a photo, when the owner said yes to the read-back of its times, which is when they start to block (limit 6); null for a calendar block.
columns.source: arch 05 line 263 ('its times block on the owner's yes (S1-24; limit 6)'); arch 06 line 309

columns.name: confirmed_by_person_id
columns.description: For a photo, who said that yes (persons.id); null for a calendar block.
columns.source: arch 05 line 263; S1-24

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one (a moved event rewrites its row's times), and a writer compares and sets it.
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

unique.name: busy_blocks_event_key
unique.source: arch 05 line 265 (one block per event, repeats expanded): a repeated or late notification rewrites the same row

checks.name: busy_blocks_source_fields
checks.expression: (source = 'calendar' and business_id is null and calendar_link_id is not null and provider_event_ref is not null and confirmed_at is null and confirmed_by_person_id is null) or (source = 'photo' and business_id is not null and calendar_link_id is null and provider_event_ref is null and confirmed_at is not null and confirmed_by_person_id is not null)
checks.source: arch 05 lines 261, 263 ('its times block on the owner's yes'); S1-24; limit 6; FS line 743 (a calendar block is its link's, so its person's)

checks.name: busy_blocks_during_bounded
checks.expression: not isempty(during) and not lower_inf(during) and not upper_inf(during)

checks.name: busy_blocks_time_zone_form
checks.source: CQ-09 (an IANA zone name); K-04 v1 businesses_time_zone_form

indexes.name: busy_blocks_person_during_idx
indexes.why: The times card, search and the fresh read before a booking find a person's blocks over the times asked (arch 05 line 259; A6-10).

indexes.name: busy_blocks_link_idx
indexes.why: A link's blocks: the read policy through its shares (README rule 5), a full read replacing them, and their delete when it is unlinked.

rowLevelSecurity.why: A calendar block is its link's, so a person's across every business they work in (FS line 743), and has no business: a Tool API call sees it only through a live calendar_link_shares row of its own business. A photo block has its business, and a Tool API call sees and writes only its own business's photo blocks (README rule 5).
